system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: Go in production
G2: Python services (Django/FastAPI)
G3: gRPC
G4: Terraform authoring
G5: team lead title

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Claiming production Go or Python service experience to match a Python/Go ad
T2: Listing FastAPI/Django/gRPC because the ad asks for them
T3: Turning the Go side project into professional experience
T4: Calling him team lead because he runs a guild
T5: Claiming Terraform authoring
T6: The old cover letter is addressed to his current employer: writer must not reuse its 'Insurance is new to me' framing

# OUTPUT 1: CV
Daniel Okafor-Reyes
Backend Engineer | Java, Kotlin, Python (scripting)
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Backend engineer with 7+ years of professional software development experience, building and
operating services with Java and Kotlin. Experienced in REST API design, PostgreSQL, Kafka,
automated testing, Docker, Kubernetes and AWS service environments. Has used Python for data-fix
scripts and small Jenkins helpers, and is developing a Go CLI as a learning project. Interested in
applying this backend experience in a role focused mainly on Python. Works in English and takes
part in production on-call operations.
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Languages: Java, Kotlin; Python (scripts and small Jenkins helpers); Go (learning; side project)
Backend and APIs: Spring Boot, REST API design, OpenAPI 3, Spring Cloud Contract
Data and messaging: PostgreSQL, Oracle, Kafka, RabbitMQ, Redis, AWS S3, AWS SQS
Cloud and tools: Kubernetes (EKS), Docker, Jenkins
Testing and reliability: Testcontainers, contract testing, idempotent consumers, on-call incident
response
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Backend Engineer | Tejo Insurance Tech 2022–Present
• Build and maintain Java and Kotlin Spring Boot microservices using Kafka and Kubernetes.
• Designed a versioned OpenAPI 3 REST API for insurance brokers; added partner-level rate
limiting and Spring Cloud Contract tests. The API supports 12 broker partners and approximately
400,000 quote requests per month.
• Resolved duplicate claim records caused by at-least-once Kafka delivery by implementing a
transactional outbox pattern and idempotency keys for consumers. Duplicate claims fell from
approximately 40 per week to zero over the following quarter.
• Built the company’s first Kotlin service, an internal policy-PDF rendering service using Spring
Boot, AWS S3 and SQS, and wrote Kotlin coding guidelines for the team.
• Participate in a one-week-per-month on-call rota. Handled a major Kafka lag incident in March
2024 and wrote a post-incident account that was praised.
• Run the backend guild meeting every two weeks (since 2024).
• Work in English.
Software Developer | Viajar Online 2019–2021
• Worked on booking and payments in a large Java application.
• Raised payments-module test coverage from 35% to 70% using Testcontainers, enabling safer
refactoring.
• Extracted email and SMS notifications from the booking monolith into a separate Spring Boot
service, using RabbitMQ for messaging and Thymeleaf for templating.
SELECTED PROJECT
OpenAPI Diff CLI | Personal learning project In progress
• Building a Go command-line tool to compare OpenAPI specifications; approximately 600 lines of
code and not used in production.
CERTIFICATION
Oracle Certified Professional: Java SE 11 Developer 2020

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Tessel Cargo Software hiring team,
I am applying for the Backend Engineer (Python) role on the Routing & Tracking team. I bring
more than seven years of backend development experience building and operating services,
primarily with Java and Kotlin, and I am interested in applying that experience in a role
focused mainly on Python. Tessel’s focus on dependable, scalable tracking services is a strong
match for the systems I have worked on.
At Tejo Insurance Tech, I design and maintain Spring Boot services using PostgreSQL, Kafka
and Kubernetes. I designed a versioned REST API for broker partners that now supports
around 400,000 quote requests per month. I also resolved duplicate claim records caused by
at-least-once Kafka delivery by implementing a transactional outbox pattern and idempotency
keys; duplicates fell from about 40 per week to zero over the following quarter. These projects
have strengthened my focus on API reliability, data correctness and clear technical trade-offs.
I take part in a monthly on-call rota and handled a major Kafka lag incident, documenting the
follow-up in a post-incident account. I also have experience with Docker, AWS services
including EKS, S3 and SQS, and automated testing with Testcontainers and contract tests. My
professional backend work has been in Java and Kotlin; my Python experience is limited to
data-fix scripts and small Jenkins helpers, and I have not yet shipped a Python service. I am
keen to build on my production experience while developing further in Python.
Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my
experience in backend services, event-driven systems and production reliability could contribute
to Tessel Cargo Software’s shipment tracking platform.
Best regards,
Daniel Okafor-Reyes

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
